Delhi Sultanate Period (1206 AD–1526 AD)

Foreign Invasions

Muhammad Bin Qasim — 1st Muslim Invasion (712 AD)

  • This invasion took place in Sindh part of India.
  • He came from Arab and killed Raja Dahir (last Hindu ruler of Sindh).
  • He was the first to introduce Jizya in Indian subcontinent.

Mahmud of Ghazni — 2nd Islamic/1st Turk Invasion (998 AD–1030 AD)

  • Turks came from Turkmenistan.
  • He attacked 17 times (1001 AD–1027 AD).
  • The first attack took place in 1001 AD, during the rule of Jayapala (Battle of Peshawar was fought between Ghaznavid army and Raja Jayapala).
  • Ghaznavi invaded Somnath in his 16th attack (1025 AD) and the 17th attack was the last attack (1027 AD).
  • Battle of Waihind: A series of conflicts between Ghazni and Hindu Shahi rulers.
  • Death: 1030 AD.
  • Court language of Turks was Persian.

#### Writers during the reign of Mahmud of Ghazni

WritersWritings
FirdausiShahnama
Al BiruniTahqiq-i-Hind (also known as Kitab-al-Hind)

Muhammad Ghori — 3rd Islamic/2nd Turk Invasion (1175 AD–1206 AD)

  • Persian name: Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad.
  • His first attack took place in: 1175 AD (in Multan) and 1178 AD in Gujarat, where he was defeated by Mularaja II, Bhima II and their mother Naikidevi.
  • Ghori attacked Delhi, which was then ruled by Prithviraj Chauhan.

Battle between Prithviraj and Ghori

  • 1st Battle of Tarain: 1191 AD (won by Prithviraj III / Prithviraj Chauhan).
  • 2nd Battle of Tarain: 1192 AD (won by Ghori). Qutb-ud-din Aibak (commander of Ghori) helped him in 2nd Battle of Tarain.
  • Jai Chand is said to have invited Md. Ghori to attack Prithviraj Chauhan.

Writer in Prithviraj's Court

  • Chandra Bardai: He wrote Prithviraj Raso (According to this epic poem, daughter of Jaichand (King of Gahadavala) Sanyogita was married to Prithviraj Chauhan).

Battle of Chandawar (1194 AD)

  • This battle was fought between Ghori and Raja Jaichand, where Ghori won the battle.
  • Slaves of Ghori: Qutb-ud-din-Aibak, Yalduz, Kubacha, Bhaktiyar Khilji (he destroyed Nalanda University).

Slave Dynasty (1206 AD–1290 AD)

  • This dynasty is also known as Mamluk Dynasty.
  • The rulers belonged to Ilbari tribe/Shamshi tribe.

Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1206 AD–1210 AD)

  • He ruled from Lahore (it was the capital city).
  • He was given the title of 'Lakh Baksh' (the giver of Lakhs).
  • Death: 1210 AD, while playing Chaugan (now known as Polo).
  • Architecture constructed by him:
  • Mosques: Quwwat-ul-Islam at Delhi and Adhai din ka Jhopra at Ajmer.
  • He also began construction of Qutub Minar (he was only able to complete the construction of basement), in honour of Sufi Saint Khwaja Qutubuddin Bhaktiyar Kaki.
  • He patronised writers like: Hasan-un-Nizami (author of Tajul-Ma'asir) and Fakhruddin.
  • Qutb-ud-din Aibak (laid foundation).
  • Iltutmish (added three more stories to it).
  • Firoz Shah Tughlaq (repaired and built the top storey).

Slave Dynasty (continued)

Shamsuddin Iltutmish (1211 AD–1236 AD)

  • He was son-in-law of Qutb-ud-din.
  • He shifted his capital from Lahore to Delhi.
  • He saved Delhi Sultanate from the wrath of Chengiz Khan (Chengiz also attacked Transoxiana region in 1219 AD. He died in 1227 AD).
  • Nizam-ul-Mulk was his Wazir (Prime Minister).
  • He patronised scholars like Minhaj-i-Siraj (wrote: Tabaquat-i-Nasiri).
  • He set up the official nobility of 40 loyal slaves known as Chahalgani. These were Turkish slaves.
  • He introduced Silver coin (Tanka) and Copper coin (Jital).
  • He introduced the Iqta system. Under this a part of land was given to military commander known as Iqtadar/Muqti.

Razia Sultana (1236 AD–1240 AD)

  • She was the daughter of Iltutmish.
  • She was the first and the only women ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
  • Altunia, Governer of Bhatinda refused to accept suzerainty of Razia. Razia and Yakut (an Ethiopian slave) marched against Altunia.
  • Altunia murdered Yakut and imprisoned Razia in Quila Mubarak of Bhatinda (Later Altunia and Razia got married).
  • In 1240 AD, Razia and Altunia became the victim of a conspiracy by Khokhar tribe and were assassinated near Kaithal (Haryana).

Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266 AD–1287 AD)

  • He was earlier a Naib under Nasiruddin Mahmud.
  • He broke the power of Chalisa (abolished Chahalgani system) and restored the prestige of the crown.
  • He established the military department Diwan-i-Arz.
  • Title taken: Zil-i-Ilahi (Shadow of Allah) and Ulugh Khan → Balban considered himself as a descendant of Afrosiyab.
  • Original name: Baha-ud-Din.
  • He introduced Sijda (prostration before the monarchy) and Paibos (kissing the feet of monarch) as the normal form of salutation.
  • He started "Blood and Iron Policy".
  • He started Nowruz (Iranian or Parsi New Year) in Delhi Sultanate.
  • Tughril Beg (Tughral Tughan Khan), the Governor of Bengal under Sultan Balban, revolted in 1279 and declared himself as an independent ruler of Bengal. Balban personally led a campaign, captured Tughril at Jajnagar, and had him executed (he became known as Tughril-Kush, "the Slayer of Tughril"). Balban himself died of natural causes in 1287.

Qaiqabad (1287 AD–1290 AD)

  • He was the last ruler of Slave Dynasty and grandson of Balban.

Important Officers

OfficerRole
WazirPrime Minister (looked after Finance Department)

AmirGovernor of Pargana

Khilji Dynasty (1290 AD–1320 AD)

  • Founder: Jalal-ud-din Khilji (1290 AD–1296 AD).

Alauddin Khilji (1296 AD–1316 AD)

  • He was the nephew of Jalal-ud-din Khilji.
  • Real name: Ali Gurshasp.
  • He held the title of Amir-i-Tuzuk (Master of Ceremonies) during the reign of Jalaluddin Khilji.
  • He abolished iqta system in the Delhi Sultanate.

Alauddin's Expeditions

  • Gujarat (1298 AD)
  • Ranthambore (1301 AD) → Then King: Hammir Dev Chauhan (Evidence of first Jauhar found during this time).
  • Mewar (1303 AD) → Capital: Chittor (King: Ratan Singh).
  • Malwa (1305 AD)
  • Jalor (1311 AD)

In Deccan

  • Alauddin's army was led by Malik Kafur (he was a eunuch).
  • He defeated:
  • Ramachandra (Yadava Dynasty ruler of Devagiri) (1308 AD)
  • Vira Ballala III (Hoysala Dynasty ruler of Dwarasamudra) (1309 AD)
  • Prataprudra Deva (Kakatiya Dynasty ruler of Warangal) (1311 AD)
  • Vira Pandya (Pandya Dynasty ruler of Madurai) (1311 AD)
  • Title taken by Alauddin after the Deccan expedition: Sikandar-i-Sani (Second Alexander).
  • Alauddin bought him from Gujarat Market at 1000 dinars, hence Malik Kafur is also known as 'Hazar Dinari'.

Court Poet Khusrau

  • Alauddin conferred the title of Tuti-e-Hind (Parrot of India) to Khusrau, his favourite court poet.
  • He started Qawwali in India.
  • Khusrau gave Sultan-e-Jahan title to Khilji.
  • His famous books: Tuglaq Nama and Nuh-i-Siphir.
  • He was the first to mention Jauhar in Persian (Khazain-ul-Futuh).

Alauddin started the system of cash payment (Naqdi) to soldiers.

Administrative Reforms Introduced by Alauddin

  • Dagh (the branding of horse) and Chehra (also known as Huliya, for identification of his soldiers).
  • Imposed heavy taxes: Ordered all lands to be measured [by Special Officer: Mustakharaj (one who collected the revenue)]. The share of state was then fixed based on this measurement.
  • Taxes Imposed: Jaziya (levied on Non-Muslims) and Zakat (levied on Muslims).
  • He introduced three new taxes: Gharai (house tax), Charai (a tax levied on use of grasslands for grazing animals), and Kharaj (a land tax imposed on peasants, amounting to 50% of their produce).

Alauddin Khilji (continued)

  • Three markets setup by Alauddin for:
  • Food grains.
  • Costly cloths → Sara-i-Adl.
  • Horses, slaves (Bandagan) and cattles.
  • Each market was under control: Shahna (high officer) who maintained a register of the merchants, shopkeeper and the prices.
  • Officer appointed to control grain market: Shahna-i-Mandi.
  • Network of spies (intelligence officers) started by Alauddin were: Munhiyans and Barid.

Alauddin formed a series of regulations to weaken the power of Nobles.

Alauddin Built

  • Alai Fort
  • Alai Darwaja (entrance of Qutub Minar)
  • Palace of thousand Pillars (Hazar Sutun)
  • Hauz Khas (tank)

He Established

  • The city Siri which was second of the seven cities of Delhi (1st city of Delhi: Qila Rai Pithora established by Tomar Dynasty).
  • Tomb of Alauddin: Delhi.
  • He was patron of Art and learning.
  • In 1316 Malik Kafur called Hajar-Dinari seized the throne after Alauddin's death.
  • Alauddin had two sons: Mubarak (1316-20 AD) and Omar. Mubarak killed Malik Kafur and Omar later.
  • Khusrau Khan: 1320 AD → Killed Mubarak and ascended the throne.

Angapala founded the Tomara Dynasty. Delhi first became the capital under their rule only.

Tughlaq Dynasty (1320 AD–1414 AD)

Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (1320 AD–25 AD)

  • Last King of Khilji Dynasty Khusrau Khan was killed by Ghazi Malik (took title: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq).
  • He built the city of Tughlaqabad and also built Tughlaqabad Fort.
  • He died in an accident and was succeeded by son Jauna (Ulugh Khan) who assumed the title Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325 AD–1351 AD)

  • He had the largest kingdom of all.
  • He was visited by traveller Ibn Battuta from Morocco who wrote a book titled "Rihla".
  • He increased taxation in Doab region in 1325 to fund his projects, including his large army.
  • He is also known as "wisest fool", due to his failed policies.
  • He transferred the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (also known as Devagiri) in 1327 and later he again reversed his decision.
  • He also gave Sondhar loan (cash in exchange of gold) and Taccavi loan as agricultural loans.

His Failed Policies

  • He introduced Token (Bronze) currency in 1329 with high value.
  • Khurasen Expedition in 1329.
  • Qarachil Expedition in 1330.

Administrative Positions

  • Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed people from variety of background to high administrative positions [mentioned by Ziauddin Barani in his book Tarikh-i-FiruzShahi (Fatwa-i-Jahandari)].
PositionPerson
A wine distillerAziz Khummar
A barberFiruz Hajjam
A cookManka Tabbakh
Two gardenersLadha and Pira
  • He also setup a agricultural department: Diwan-i-Kohi.
  • He built the city of Jahanpanah.

Begumpuri Mosque: It was built during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351 AD–1388 AD)

  • He was the cousin of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.
  • Imposed four kinds of taxes mentioned in Quran:
  • Kharaj: Land tax = 1/10 of the produce.
  • Zakat: 2% tax on property.
  • Jizya: Levied on Non-Muslims.
  • Khams: 1/5th of the booty captured during war.
  • He collected Jizya as a separate tax.
  • The soldiers were not paid in cash but by assignments on land revenue of villagers known as Vajha.
  • He repaired number of canals and imposed: Haque-i-Sharb (irrigation tax) and Hasil-i-Sharb (water tax).
  • He built new cities: Fatehabad, Hisar, Jaunpur (in the name of Muhammed bin Tughlaq (Jauna), Firozabad.
  • He was the first Sultan in India who started the work of translation of Hindu Religious texts into the Persian language.
  • He established a hospital at Delhi: Dar-ul-Shifa
  • New department set up by him: Diwan-i-Khairat (for the needs of poor and needy) and Diwan-i-Bandagan (Department of Slaves).
  • His PM was: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.
  • Iqta system made hereditary during his reign.

Timur Invasion (1398 AD)

  • He was a mongoloid.
  • He invaded during the reign of last ruler of Tughlaq Dynasty → Mahmud Shah Tughlaq.

Sayyid Dynasty (1414 AD–1451 AD)

  • Founder: Khizr Khan (1414 AD–1421 AD) → Title taken: Rayat-e-Ala.
  • They were known as "Kulah-Daran" (cap wearers).
  • After defeating the army of Delhi in 1398, Timur appointed Khizr Khan as the ruler of Multan. Khizr Khan defeated Sultan Daulat Khan and occupied Delhi and founded Sayyid dynasty.
  • Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi written by Yahya-bin-Ahmad Sirhindi, where he tells that Sayyids were the descendants of Prophet Muhammed.

Lodi Dynasty (1451 AD–1526 AD)

  • Lodi's were of Afghan origin.
  • Founder: Bahlol Lodi (1451 AD–1489 AD).

Sikandar Lodi (1489 AD–1517 AD)

  • He is also known as Nizam Shah.
  • He founded Agra in 1504 and later made it his capital in 1506.
  • He introduced: Gaz-i-Sikandari (Sikandari's yard) of 32 digits to measure cultivated fields.
  • He was a poet and composed poems in Persian, under the name Gulrukhi.
  • He gave orders to build: Moth ki Masjid (in Delhi).

Ibrahim Lodi (1517 AD–1526 AD)

  • He was the last ruler of Delhi Sultanate.
  • Babur was invited to attack on Ibrahim Lodi by Daulat Khan Lodi, who was the governor of Punjab under Ibrahim Lodi.
  • He fought and lost the Battle of Panipat against Babur in 1526 AD.
